args.query: inactive replication slot WAL disk full postgres
replication slot retaining WAL disk full

events.statement: payment-service error rate jumped from ~0.23% to ~61% at the 15:00 bucket and stayed elevated through 16:50 (last value 63.76%).
payment-service payment success rate collapsed from ~99% to ~35% at 15:00 and remained at ~35% through 16:45.
payment-service ERROR logs are dominated by ledger write failures 'No space left on device', first seen 15:00:26, 354 matches, continuing to 16:57:54.
ledger-db disk_used_pct rose monotonically from 78.23% at 11:00 to 100% at 15:02 and stayed pegged at 100% through 16:59.
ledger-db logs repeatedly report replication slot 'analytics_cdc' is inactive; retaining tens of GB of WAL, from 12:19 (63157 MB) up to 91901 MB, earliest seen 13:02, recurring until 14:49.
ledger-db emitted disk-usage warnings climbing 90% (13:10) -> 95% (14:15) -> 98% (14:48), then PANIC/ERROR 'No space left on device' writing pg_wal and base files from 15:01:01.
order-service, which does not run payment-service's code, also logs INSERT failures 'No space left on device' starting 15:00:42 (236 matches) — matching the ledger-db saturation window.
Only one deployment in the window: payment-service v6.0.0 deployed 14:46 (new UPI mandate flow, ledger entry type MANDATE_HOLD), rolled back at 15:12; no config/flag changes occurred.
ledger-db is a shared postgres used by order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service and settlement-service.
Prior incident HIST-114 (2025-04-18) on ledger-db had the same pattern: 'Inactive replication slot retained WAL until disk filled', resolved by dropping the slot.
payment-service error rate stayed ~61-64% well after the 15:12 rollback (e.g. avg 63.57 at 16:20), i.e. the rollback did not reduce errors.

Interpretation: the fault originates in the shared ledger-db storage, whose disk was exhausted by WAL retained by the inactive analytics_cdc replication slot; payment-service's v6.0.0 deploy is temporally near but causally unrelated.
